clue.text: Computer key sometimes made by prisoners

definitions.meaning: the Esc key at the top left of a keyboard, used to back out of a command
a breakout from jail is what some inmates manage

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same word: the keyboard's Esc button and a getaway from confinement.

clue.text: It's. attractive, coming into battle

explanation.definitionFit: The word means charming, and is also the participle of joining battle with an enemy.

clue.text: Team up with copper, arresting northern girl

indicators.note: the coin holds the others, as police arrest and hold someone

parts.note: a copper is a low-value coin
Jo is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A policeman nabs a northern girl and teams up with her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer or the metal CU; it is a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To conjoin is to join together or unite, so to team up with.

clue.text: Verse once kept within safe bounds

indicators.note: the verse goes inside the safe

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
rime is an archaic spelling of rhyme, verse

explanation.surface: Old poetry stored inside secure limits.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter for a safe is thieves' slang, as in 'peterman' for a safebreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The perimeter is the boundary line around an area, its bounds.

clue.text: Formalities Blimp's image promoter observed?

parts.note: a PR man, a pro, promotes an image
belonging to Colonel Blimp, the cartoon reactionary, is 'to Col', Col being the short form of Colonel

explanation.surface: A publicist for the pompous Colonel Blimp kept to the formalities.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp was a British cartoon figure of blustering conservatism; what is Blimp's is, playfully, 'to Col'. 'Observed?' sets the scene of etiquette being kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the code of formal etiquette, so the word covers official formalities.

clue.text: Relax, bringing a row to an end?

definitions.meaning: stop working and take a break

definitions.text: bringing a row to an end?
definitions.meaning: rowers ending their session literally stop pulling at the blades

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to pause after effort, and literally describes rowers ceasing to pull.

clue.text: Fearful idiot loses 'wife when climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing reads the remainder from the bottom upwards
the wife letter is lost from the idiot

parts.note: a dimwit is a stupid person

explanation.surface: A frightened fool loses his wife while mountaineering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes W from DIMWIT, leaving DIMIT; 'when climbing' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Timid means lacking courage, easily frightened.

clue.text: One in church opposed to alcoholic drink

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the run of pieces

parts.note: anti means against
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A churchgoer who is against booze.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany, so an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Start to lock a box, having lost pounds in recent times

indicators.note: the start of each word gives its first letter, and the one-letter word a is its own start
the pounds letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: the box is British slang for television, the telly
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Someone starts to lock a strongbox, having recently lost money.
explanation.walkthrough: The L from 'lock' is a separate piece, not the one 'having lost' takes from TELLY, which leaves TELY; 'box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Lately is an adverb meaning recently, in the recent past.

clue.text: Propose issue should carry music article

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece carries those above it

parts.note: pop is popular music
the is the definite article
an issue is a question for debate

explanation.surface: A matter of debate ought to include an article on music.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose marriage is idiomatically to ask the big question.

clue.text: Huge trap set by soldiers cut off rodent's tail

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for game
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: a tail cut off means the word loses its final letter
names the end of the word as the part cut away

parts.note: a mouse is a small rodent

explanation.surface: A trap laid by soldiers has severed some rodent's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off' with 'tail' removes the last letter of MOUSE, leaving MOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginormous is informal British slang for enormously large, a blend of gigantic and enormous.

clue.text: One's witty saying about damp

indicators.note: the witty saying goes round the other piece, standing about it

parts.note: a mot (bon mot) is a witty remark
one is I, and 'one's' is 'one is', I'S

explanation.surface: Someone's clever quip concerns dampness.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist and damp are synonyms for slightly wet.

clue.text: Ring German commander left out in luxury car

indicators.note: the trimmed name goes inside the car abbreviation

parts.note: GT is gran turismo, a high-performance touring car

indicators.note: signals that the left letter is taken out of the commander's name

parts.note: Erwin Rommel, the Second World War German field marshal

explanation.surface: A ring-shaped item has the German general left out in a smart car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call or jewellery; it is the definition. 'out' signals the deletion of the left letter from the field marshal's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A grommet is a metal or rubber eyelet ring that reinforces a hole.

clue.text: Landor, I fancy, may be first

indicators.note: to fancy is to imagine freely, so the letters are reimagined in a new order

explanation.surface: Walter Savage Landor, I imagine, might come first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges LANDOR plus I. The definition is by example: 'first' is one such number word.
explanation.definitionFit: First, second and third are ordinal numbers, words giving position in a sequence.

clue.text: Music representing a certain person in Holy Writ

indicators.note: the person goes inside the scripture abbreviation

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, part of Holy Writ
'one' stands for a person, as in 'one should'

explanation.surface: Music portraying an individual from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a piece of music written for nine performers.

clue.text: Mysterious English drunkard fine once in Ireland

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drinker
an eric was the blood fine paid for a killing under old Irish law

explanation.surface: An Englishman, a drunk, was fined long ago in Ireland in strange circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is obscure, understood only by a few initiates, hence mysterious.

clue.text: Vigorous fellow accepting contract to support printing unit

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower part supports the one on top

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of measure

indicators.note: the name takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: Eric is a man's name, a fellow
to contract an illness is to get it

explanation.surface: An energetic chap accepts a deal to back a printing unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Energetic means full of energy, active and vigorous.

clue.text: Concur with writer about colour of Lear's boat

indicators.note: the writer goes around the other piece

parts.note: a pen is something to write with
to concur is to agree

explanation.surface: Agree with an author on the hue of a famous poet's vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear's Owl and the Pussy-cat went to sea in a beautiful pea-green boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear's nonsense poem names this pale green shade for the boat, so the phrase describes it.

clue.text: Opening a fresh container of water?

parts.note: fresh in the sense of cheeky, pert
the Ure is a Yorkshire river, playfully a channel holding water

explanation.surface: A gap created by a new water tank, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful idea of a river as a container of water: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a hole or gap, an opening that lets light or air through.

clue.text: Girl has fuchsia finally replaced by border plant

indicators.note: the letter is swapped out for the border word

parts.note: Paula is a girl's name

indicators.note: takes the last letter of fuchsia

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A girl has her fuchsia replaced at last with a border plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letter of fuchsia is A; the first A of PAULA becomes RIM. 'border plant' looks like one phrase, but 'border' is RIM.
explanation.definitionFit: The primula is a genus of flowering plants including primroses and cowslips.

clue.text: Clothe bear right away

indicators.note: says the right letter goes away from the verb

parts.note: to bear something is to endure it

explanation.surface: Dress the bear immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'at once'; it is R plus a deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Endue is a literary verb meaning to invest or dress someone, as with a garment or quality.

clue.text: Slaver taking drudges originally on river

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the letter on top of the river
originally means at the start, so the first letter

parts.note: the Ribble is a river in Lancashire, northern England

explanation.surface: A slave-trader takes drudgers to a river first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slaver' looks like a slave trader; here it is the verb to drool.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaver is to let saliva run from the mouth, just as to dribble is.

clue.text: Old fogey Londoners associate, with Leicester

definitions.meaning: Leicester ... is a famous London ... in the West End

explanation.definitionFit: A square is a conventional old-fashioned person, and also the open space in Leicester's London name.

clue.text: Leave America without initially, earning discharge

indicators.note: outside, so these pieces enclose the letter

parts.note: to quit is to leave

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of earning

parts.note: US is the United States

explanation.surface: Quit the States without earning a severance payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A quietus is a release or discharge, originally the acquittance of a debt, and figuratively death.

clue.text: Doctor providing free entertainment

definitions.meaning: to give medical care to, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to give medical care, and also an outing or meal paid for by someone else.

clue.text: Continuing to operate just after departing

parts.note: 'on' can mean immediately following, as in 'on arrival'
going means leaving or departing

explanation.surface: Still working right up to the moment of leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ongoing is still in progress, carrying on rather than ended.

clue.text: Entertain a sister goddess

parts.note: the nine Muses were sister goddesses of the arts

explanation.surface: Keep a goddess, one of several sisters, amused.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse is to entertain or divert someone.

clue.text: Crabby woman in Irish ballet taking regular parts

indicators.note: the woman goes inside the other pieces
regular parts means every other letter, here the first, third and fifth

parts.note: Rita is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A grumpy woman in an Irish ballet company takes regular roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking regular parts' picks every other letter of ballet, starting with the first; 'in' puts the woman's name inside the Irish abbreviation plus those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby and irritable are synonyms for bad-tempered and easily annoyed.

clue.text: Former stage work making great demands

parts.note: ex means former
acting is work on the stage

explanation.surface: A former stage career that was very demanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Exacting means requiring great effort or precision, hence demanding.

clue.text: Directions covering American Indian broadcast on TV

indicators.note: the directions sit either side, covering the people

parts.note: S and N are south and north, compass directions
S and N are south and north, compass directions
the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: Instructions about a Native American programme shown on television.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen a programme is to show or transmit it on television.
